final_claim.narrative: Comparing the two half-windows around t=79269 ([74269,79269] vs [79269,84269]) shows that a large set of external partners (the same 30-node set) is present in both periods: before it was served by nodes 728 and 785 (step_09, step_10), and after the same partner set is served by nodes 898 and 1269 (step_23, step_24). The total event counts for the group are similar in the two half-windows (148 vs 143; step_04), and the group members are among the top-active nodes in the full interval (step_02). Only a few small partner changes appear (e.g. 357→508 present before only, 381→1710 present after; steps_06 and _19), consistent with limited background turnover or reassignment within the group rather than an abrupt wholesale replacement of the group's contact set. Therefore there is no strong temporal signature of an abrupt regime-style replacement of partners; instead the same partner set persists while responsibility for contacting them shifts among group members.
